sections.heading: Modal verbs for possibility
sections.body: Modal verbs express how certain we are about something. They do not change form and are followed by the base verb.

sections.heading: Degrees of certainty
table: She must be tired. She worked all day.

sections.heading: Might / May / Could
sections.body: These express different degrees of possibility. They mean 'perhaps'.
list: It might rain later. (possible)
She may be at home. (possible)
He could be the new manager. (possible)
They might not come to the party. (possible negative)

sections.heading: Must for deduction
sections.body: Use 'must' when you are almost sure something is true because of the evidence.
list: She has not eaten all day. She must be hungry.
The lights are on. They must be at home.
He works 12 hours a day. He must be tired.

sections.heading: Can't for impossibility
sections.body: Use 'can't' when you are sure something is NOT true.
list: He can't be at home. I saw him leave.
That can't be true. It's impossible.
She can't be 50. She looks 30.

sections.heading: Common mistakes
list: Do not use 'to' after modals: 'She must to be tired' is wrong.
Do not confuse 'must' (deduction) with 'must' (obligation). Context decides.
Do not use 'can' for deduction; use 'can't' for impossibility.

list.definition: It may snow in the mountains.
Look at the snow. It must be cold.
It can't be hot in December.
I'm not sure. He might be late.
I think she must be tired.
Look at the sky. It might rain.
There's a chance he will come.
I'm sure she must be at home.
I'm certain he can't be serious.

phases.name: Discovery
phases.intro: Look at these sentences. Read them carefully and think about the questions below.
sentences: She has not eaten all day. She must be hungry.
He might be at home. I'm not sure.
That can't be true. It's impossible.
It may rain later this afternoon.
He could be the new manager.
The lights are on. They must be at home.
He can't be at home. I saw him leave.
They might not come to the party.
questions: In sentence 1, why do we use 'must'?
In sentences 2, 4 and 5, what do 'might', 'may' and 'could' express?
In sentences 3 and 7, why do we use 'can't'?
In sentence 6, what is the evidence for the deduction?
In sentence 8, how do we make a negative possibility?

questions.prompt: She has not eaten all day. She ___ be hungry.
questions.explanation: When we are sure about something, we use must.

questions.prompt: He ___ be at home. I saw him leave five minutes ago.
questions.explanation: When something is impossible, we use cannot.

questions.prompt: It ___ rain later. The sky is cloudy.
The lights are on. They ___ be at home.
That story ___ be true. It's impossible.
She ___ be the new manager. I'm not sure.
He works 12 hours a day. He ___ be tired.
They ___ not come to the party. They are busy.
She ___ be 50. She looks 30.
It's very cold. It ___ snow tonight.

phases.name: Free practice
prompts: Your friend is not answering the phone. Write 5 possible reasons using might, may, could.
Look at a photo of a stranger and write 5 deductions using must, might, can't.
Write 5 sentences about tomorrow's weather using different modal verbs (might, may, could, must, can't).

questions.prompt: She has a big smile. She ___ be very happy.
He ___ be at the office. He is on holiday.
It ___ rain. Take an umbrella.
The car is very old. It ___ break down soon.
He speaks 5 languages. He ___ be very intelligent.
That ___ be Sarah. She is in Paris.
She ___ come to the party. She is not sure.
You have been running. You ___ be tired.
They ___ be at the beach. It's raining.
I ___ go to the cinema tonight. I haven't decided.

sections.heading: Key rules
list: Must: strong deduction based on evidence.
Might / May / Could: possibility.
Can't: impossibility.
Modals do not change form and are followed by the base verb.

sections.heading: Common mistakes
list: Do not use 'to' after modals.
Do not use 'can' for deduction; use 'can't' for impossibility.
Do not confuse 'must' (deduction) with 'must' (obligation).

sections.heading: Useful phrases
list: She must be...
He might be...
It could be...
They can't be...
I'm not sure, but...
Perhaps... / Maybe...
